subject: Electrical Engineering
title: Nuclear Power: Splitting Atoms
description: A quick win: understand Nuclear Power: Splitting Atoms.

hook.text: One kilogram of uranium holds as much energy as 2,700 tonnes of coal.

buildup.text: Fission splits heavy atoms. The fragments fly apart and release immense heat.

discovery.text: That heat boils water into steam — the rest works like any thermal plant.

twist.text: Nuclear produces zero carbon emissions during operation. Waste is tiny but dangerous.

climax.text: About 10% of the world's electricity comes from 440 nuclear reactors.

punchline.text: Split an atom and a city lights up.

quiz.question: Why does nuclear power produce no carbon emissions during operation?
options: It uses solar panels alongside the reactor
Fission releases heat from atomic bonds, not from burning carbon fuels
Carbon is captured and stored underground automatically
